4. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. The case of defendant No. 1, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. It is barred by limitation, it is also bad for defect of parties. The further case of defendant No. 1 is that he married plaintiff No. 1 in the year 1973, but she was not interested to live with defendant No. 1. While defendant No. 1 was serving in Bangladesh Army, plaintiff No. 1 left the house of defendant No. 1 without permission of his parents. Plaintiff No. 1 was unwilling to perform her part of marital obligation. Plaintiff No. 2 was under the custody of defendant No. 1 and in order to rear her up defendant No. 1 again married to one Kabita Rani. Plaintiff No. 1 finally left the house of defendant No. 1 on 20-4-1997 and since then there was no conjugal relationship between them. Plaintiff No. 3 is not the daughter of defendant No. 1 and, as such, defendant No. 1 is not bound to maintain her. Since plaintiff No. 1 does not perform her part of marital obligation, she is not entitled to maintenance. For the reasons stated, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 5. On the pleadings, various issues were framed including maintainability of the suit, limitation and whether or not plaintiffs were entitled to reliefs as prayed for.
